To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
choline and its derivatives play a crucial role in brain function, and that choline-containing phosphatides are effective compounds for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases.

1) choline and CCPLs are involved in brain functional pathways, 2) CCPLs exert neuroprotective effects in experimental models of neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular disorders, 3) CCPLs are effective in the treatment of cognitive impairment associated with cerebrovascular disorders and in the treatment of mild cognitive impairment associated with Alzheimer’s disease.
“CDP-choline and choline alphoscerta are effective in the treatment of cognitive disorders characterized by choline neurotransmitter deficit”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying the beneficial effects of selected CCPLs in brain diseases and their translation into clinical practice.

the identification of the molecular targets of CCPLs, the elucidation of their mechanisms of action, the identification of the most appropriate CCPLs for clinical studies, the design of the most appropriate study protocol and the evaluation of their efficacy in clinical studies.
the role of CCPLs in brain metabolism and the effects of exogenous administration of selected compounds in animal models and in patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
choline and choline-containing PLs have the potential to be effective therapeutic compounds for the treatment of cognitive impairment.
CCPLs, especially citicoline and GPC, could be a promising therapeutic approach for the management of cognitive impairment in neurodegenerative diseases.

CCPLs are not only important for the brain as precursors of acetylcholines and structural elements of cell membranes but they may also play a role in the pathophysiology and therapy of some brain disorders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cholinergic hypothesis of dementia and cholinergic deficit in neurodegenerative diseases is not the only one, but it could be one of the many pathways that are involved in the pathophysiology of neurodegenerative and neurovascular diseases.
CCPLs are a class of compounds with a wide range of biological activities, and their effects on brain function are mediated by different pathways.
CCPLs have a role in the brain and could be useful in brain disorders characterized with cholinergic neurotransmitter deficit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
choline is an essential nutrient and its availability is critical for brain health.
CCPLs could be considered for the treatment of cognitive symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.
choline and choline-containing PLs are involved in the pathophysiology of several brain disorders, and their therapeutic potential has not been fully exploited.
